I see a lot of finger pointing at Greece here. This is a very capitalistic view point IMO. If you take your capitalistic views out of the equation and just look at it from other angles, I think you might see some things worth discussing.

For a good while investors saw Greece as a money making machine. Again, I'm talking investment wise. They were actively encouraged to borrow, borrow, borrow. The people encouraging them sought to make a profit from them going into debt, and they did... a lot of profit.

They are in fact still trying to do so. Before Greece could see what was happening it was in so deep there was no escape. Even the I.M.F. says that there is no hope for Greece without writing off some of their debt. Their debt is approaching 200% of their GDP, and it gets worse every day as their economy shrinks due to force policy changes.

To empathize with Greece you have to understand a few things that require giving them the benefit of the doubt.
1. They know they are wrong.
2. They feel the world has pushed and cheated them.
3. They DO want to do the right thing.
4. They feel trapped with no escape and no right answer.

They feel they are literally in a situation of damned if you do, damned if you don't. There are two reasons they don't want to borrow money again. The first is that they have already done austerity and it not only didn't help, it made it worse, A LOT worse. To have people try to shove more austerity down their throats is offensive to them. They feel as if they are not being treated fairly as an equal member. The second reason is that their problems are derived from borrowing money, so why borrow more? They feel at some point it has to stop. More so considering that they have already tried borrowing money to make it better.

So why did they make a deal? Because they have to choose the lesser of two evils. Greece's only hope is to try to kick the can long enough for someone to actually give a shit and give them some real help. The capitalist view is to NEVER write off debt, but this is so extreme there is literally no other option that will save Greece from default. If not now, it will just happen in the future.

Is Greece blameless. Absolutely not. They could have not done what they did. It was in their power to not do it. From my perspective, at least they are owning up to their blame, but because of capitalism, everyone else doesn't feel obligated to share the blame for pushing REALLY hard to make them do it.

As an American, I would be devastated if my country were in that position. I would feel embarrassed and ashamed. So I for one don't hate on Greece. Sometimes you really do need to just cut your losses and help a friend.
